clue.text: Where you'll find king, queen or bishop, and second of pawns in position

definitions.text: Where you'll find king, queen or bishop

indicators.note: the picked letter goes inside the word for position

parts.note: a place is a position or spot

indicators.note: asks for the second letter of the word pawns

parts.note: the second letter of the word pawns

explanation.surface: A chess lesson listing the pieces and where a pawn stands on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess setting makes you think of a board; but kings, queens and bishops (the clergy) can all be found in a palace.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace is the official residence of a monarch or a bishop, so royalty and senior clergy live there.

clue.text: Long ago, they ruled islands in sound

indicators.note: the islands' name is spoken, giving the answer's pronunciation

parts.note: the Faroes are an island group in the North Atlantic

explanation.surface: A history of rulers of islands, or of islands set in a stretch of water.
explanation.walkthrough: Sound looks like a sea channel around the islands; it signals speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Pharaohs were the kings of ancient Egypt, rulers of thousands of years ago.

clue.text: Circus performer who has some pride in his act

definitions.text: Circus performer who has some pride in his act

parts.words: Circus performer who has some pride in his act
parts.note: pride reads as self-respect in one's work, but a pride is a group of lions appearing in the act

explanation.walkthrough: Pride reads as satisfaction in one's work; a pride is also a family group of lions.
explanation.definitionFit: A lion-tamer is a circus performer who trains and controls lions in the ring.

clue.text: Body of animal without tail found outside a South American city

indicators.note: the shortened word goes around the a
the last letter of that word is dropped

parts.note: a carcass is the dead body of an animal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tailless animal corpse turns up on the edge of a city in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Caracas is the capital city of Venezuela.

clue.text: British cargo transporter in shady cove

parts.note: a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge that carries cargo to and from ships

explanation.surface: A British barge moored in a dark sheltered inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: Cove looks like a bay, but in British slang a cove is a chap; a blighter is a contemptible fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Blighter is British slang for a rotten fellow, and a shady cove is a disreputable man.

clue.text: Curbed two people, it's said, in this business

parts.note: something curbed is limited or restricted
the saying goes: two's company, three's a crowd

explanation.surface: Two people were held back in a firm, so the story goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A limited company is a business whose owners' liability is limited to their shares.

clue.text: Broken finger restricting you, we hear, in use of arms

indicators.note: the reworked letters enclose the you letter
a broken word has its letters scattered and reassembled

parts.note: the letter U is pronounced like the word you

explanation.surface: A broken finger keeps you from handling weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: Arms suggests limbs beside the finger; it means weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunfire is the repeated shooting of guns, the use of firearms.

clue.text: What Basie and Ellington each had? Right

definitions.text: What Basie and Ellington each had
definitions.meaning: first meaning: Count Basie and Duke Ellington each bore a noble rank as a name

explanation.walkthrough: The jazz bandleaders were known as Count Basie and Duke Ellington, both nobles' ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is an honorific rank like Count or Duke, and also a legal claim of ownership.

clue.text: Root crop recipe's one thing to eat

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe, take
a dish is a prepared item of food

explanation.surface: A recipe whose key ingredient is a vegetable grown underground.
explanation.definitionFit: The radish is a plant grown for its crisp, pungent edible root.

clue.text: Judged badly, but not excessively

parts.note: a misjudgement that erred on the low side, under rather than over

explanation.walkthrough: The second half sounds like softening the criticism; it tells you which way the misjudgement went.
explanation.definitionFit: To underestimate is to rate something lower than it really is.

clue.text: Time before noon, when husband's away, for affair

parts.note: a.m. stands for ante meridiem, before midday

indicators.note: the husband being away means his letter leaves the word for time

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy and marriage records

explanation.surface: A morning tryst arranged while the husband is out of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: An amour is a love affair, especially a secret or illicit one.

clue.text: Remarked about male in area being proposed as candidate

indicators.note: the word for remarked goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to note something is to remark on it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone commenting on a man from the district who is up for election.
explanation.definitionFit: To be nominated is to be formally put forward for election or an office.

clue.text: Object a tiny bit after front page is removed

indicators.note: that letter is dropped from the word for a tiny bit

parts.note: a particle is a minute piece of something

indicators.note: takes the leading letter of the word page

parts.note: the first letter of page, also its usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone objecting to a little item appearing after the front page is cut from a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper picture makes article look like it means a news story, but here it is a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: An article is a particular item or thing, as in an article of clothing.

clue.text: Muscle of pugilist initially wrapped by seconds

indicators.note: that letter sits inside the word for seconds

parts.note: a trice is a very short moment, so trices are seconds

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of the word pugilist

parts.note: the first letter of pugilist, a boxer

explanation.surface: A boxer's muscle being strapped up by the corner-men between rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Seconds suggests the boxer's corner team; it means brief moments.
explanation.definitionFit: The triceps is the large muscle at the back of the upper arm.

clue.text: Original paths made by PM once in London park

indicators.note: an original arrangement of these letters is a new one, so the words are reworked

parts.note: Edward Heath was British Prime Minister 1970-74

explanation.surface: A former prime minister laid out the first footpaths in a park in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampstead Heath is a large open park in north London.
explanation.definitionFit: Hampstead Heath is a well-known area of ancient parkland in north London.

clue.text: Lack of originality seen in special interests

indicators.note: a special arrangement is an unusual one, so the letters of interests are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone's special interests turn out to be boringly unoriginal.
explanation.definitionFit: Triteness is the quality of being hackneyed or overused, lacking freshness.

clue.text: Fish in small can poet finishes

indicators.note: the poet's name comes at the end

parts.note: a tin is a can
Thomas Gray wrote the Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard

explanation.surface: A poet polishes off a little tinned fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat sea fish with a venomous spine on its tail.

clue.text: What's characteristic about diamonds I catalogued? Resistant to change

indicators.note: the word for characteristic goes around the diamonds letter

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic feature
taken as written
something catalogued is on a list

explanation.surface: A jeweller asking what is typical about the diamonds they have listed.
explanation.walkthrough: D is the card abbreviation for diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditionalist adheres to established customs and opposes innovation.

clue.text: It's radio, mostly, that's ruined this record producer

indicators.note: the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only most of the word radio is used, losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone complaining that radio has ruined the music producer's career.
explanation.walkthrough: Record producer suggests the music business; a diarist produces a written record.
explanation.definitionFit: A diarist keeps a daily written account, so produces a personal record of events.

clue.text: Performer, a couple of times, separately covered by a wage increase

indicators.note: each time letter sits inside the a-plus-rise word, at a different place
the two time letters go in at different places, not side by side

parts.note: taken as written
a rise is a pay increase in British usage
a couple of times asks for two T letters; this is the first of the pair
T is the abbreviation for time, here the second letter of the pair

explanation.surface: A performer twice gets a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: The two T letters go in at different places, which is what separately signals.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer such as a singer or dancer.

clue.text: Pub set up drink outside, ready for ploughman

indicators.note: the drink word goes around the reversed pub word

parts.note: ale is beer

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a bar is a pub or drinking room

explanation.surface: A pub lays on beer outdoors for a farm worker; a ploughman's is a British pub lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Arable land is suitable for ploughing and growing crops.

clue.text: Make a recovery as result of doctoring miracle

indicators.note: doctoring something means tampering with it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient recovers thanks to a medical miracle.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctoring and recovery suggest medicine; the recovery is of something lost.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim is to retrieve or recover something previously lost or given up.

clue.text: Ask for money, having daughter imprisoned?

indicators.note: the cage word has the daughter letter held within it

parts.note: to cage someone is to imprison them; the question mark hints the daughter is the one locked up

explanation.surface: A parent begs for cash after a daughter is jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: Caged plus D would give the imprisoned sense; here the daughter herself is placed inside, as the question mark hints.
explanation.definitionFit: To cadge is to scrounge or beg money from someone.

clue.text: Model gets right into hit number

parts.note: to pat is to hit lightly

indicators.note: the right letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: A fashion model is lucky enough to land a hit song.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern is a model or template from which something is copied.

clue.text: Venue for one sport or another

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... in Gloucestershire hosts famous horse trials
second meaning: the racket game played with a shuttlecock

explanation.walkthrough: Badminton House, an English country estate, holds a major annual equestrian event; the racket sport is named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name serves for the estate hosting horse trials and for the shuttlecock game.

clue.text: Sonneteer, oddly enough, making contemptuous remark

indicators.note: keep the odd-numbered letters of the word Sonneteer

parts.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters of this nine-letter word

explanation.surface: A poet who, strangely, makes a disdainful comment.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneer is a scornful remark or expression of disdain.

clue.text: After competition I had little energy — it's just before nightfall

indicators.note: the I had piece comes after the competition word

parts.note: an event is a contest in a sports programme
I'd is the contraction of I had
a little energy is just its abbreviation, E

explanation.surface: An athlete says they were exhausted after the contest, just as night was falling.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventide is a poetic word for evening, the time as day turns to night.

clue.text: This river, from the headwater, reaches large estuary, ultimately

indicators.note: take the final letter of each of these words

parts.words: from the headwater, reaches large estuary
parts.note: the final letters of these six words, read in order

explanation.surface: A river flowing from its source until it finally reaches a broad estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mersey is the river through Liverpool, which does end in a wide estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mersey is a river in north-west England that flows into the Irish Sea.
